## How to use this doc

Same convention as `docs/build/v1.5-post-ship-audit.md`: each item is self-contained. Per CLAUDE.md, state model/effort + rationale before editing, keep the build green, add tier-1 tests alongside sync/money logic, one green commit per item, **no commit/push without explicit permission**. Update each item's **Status** line as work progresses, and add the commit hash when done.

**Status legend:** `TODO` · `NEEDS DECISION` · `NEEDS INVESTIGATION` · `IN PROGRESS` · `FIXED (uncommitted)` · `DONE <hash>`

Suggested build order, re-sequenced 2026-07-04 for Alvin's **solo on-device self-test cadence** (see "Testing workflow" below — he builds and tests each item himself before it's committed, so the order front-loads quick, highly visible, easy-to-verify wins and defers items that need external setup or live investigation): **1 → 10 → 4 → 5 → 8 → 11 → 2 → 12 → 3 → 9 → 6/7**, then the 2026-07-05 additions: **14 → 13 → 15** (14 first since both 13 and 15 are cleaner to build against its new nav shape than to retrofit afterward; 14 and 15 both need a `/grilling` pass first).

Rationale, grouped into phases:
- **Phase 1 — trivial "look and confirm" wins:** 1 (already `DONE fa3bff4`), 10 (Private-toggle caption, one file), 4 (navbar editor filter), 5 (Beta settings section + Upcoming page, pure content). Each is verified by glancing at a screen — good for building momentum, one clean commit each.
- **Phase 2 — self-contained logic, crisp pass/fail:** 8 (PIN lockout — wrong-PIN counter + cooldown, has unit tests, no cross-feature entanglement).
- **Phase 3 — Analysis + Records (hard-ordered):** 11 (Analysis presets — adds bucket types to `AnalysisPeriodRange`), then 2 (Records month window). **2 MUST come after 11** — it extracts the shared month math into `core/date/MonthWindow.kt`, and doing it after 11's additions land avoids re-touching that extraction twice. This is the one hard dependency in the doc.
- **Phase 4 — heavier money path:** 12 (transfer fee — linked expense + schema change + balance math; do it warmed up on the transaction path from Item 10).
- **Phase 5 — needs external setup to test:** 3 (forgot password — Supabase dashboard email-template redirect config + an email round-trip to verify the deep link), 9 (version gate — needs the `app_release_info` row created + a deliberately-mismatched build to observe the block). Deferred here because they can't be verified by a plain on-device glance the way Phases 1–2 can.
- **Phase 6 — investigation, not a clean build:** 6/7 (biometric — root cause still unknown; needs a live device repro with Logcat before a fix is scoped; 7 is almost certainly a duplicate of 6, close it when 6's fix restores biometric-first).

**Deviations from the earlier post-grilling order** (`1 → 9 → 4 → 8 → 10 → 3 → 11 → 2 → 12 → 6/7 → 5`): 9 moved way down — its "do early so testers stay on the iterated build" rationale doesn't apply to a solo self-test loop, and it's awkward to verify alone (needs a Supabase row + a mismatched build). 5 moved way up — it's the easiest zero-dependency visible win, ideal early. 3 moved down next to 9 since both need external setup. The `11 → 2` and `6/7`-last constraints are preserved.

### Testing workflow (Alvin, v1.6.1)

Alvin drives the on-device testing himself — do **not** assume the emulator loop runs each slice. Per-item cadence:
1. Claude builds the slice green (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` for any tier-1 logic).
2. Alvin runs `./gradlew assembleStagingDebug`, installs the APK (`app/build/outputs/apk/staging/debug/`) on his **real device**, and tests by hand. `stagingDebug` hits the **staging** Supabase (where the `testdev2-5@iponlove.com` accounts + live schema are) and installs as `com.iponlove.app.staging`, alongside the Play install. Both flavors set `IS_BETA_BUILD = true`, so beta-gated items (1, 5, 9) are visible in `stagingDebug`.
3. When Alvin is satisfied, and only then, Claude commits (with explicit permission each time). Rebuilding the APK many times is independent of commits.
4. This repeats across all items until Alvin is satisfied with the whole of v1.6.1.
5. **Ship:** bump `versionName = "1.6.1"` / `versionCode = 3` (`app/build.gradle.kts:28-29`), `./gradlew bundleProdRelease`, upload the AAB. If Item 9 shipped, set the Supabase `required_version_code` row to `3` at ship time (exact-match gate would otherwise block Alvin/testers).

## Item 1 — Beta feedback screen shows a misleading "(prod)" version tag

- **Status:** DONE fa3bff4
- **Severity:** Low (cosmetic, but actively misleading to beta testers)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low

**What was wrong:** `BetaFeedbackViewModel` built the prefilled Google Form URL using `BuildConfig.FLAVOR`, which is `"prod"` for the Play Console internal-testing build — because Play Console locked the app listing's `applicationId` to the `prod` flavor (see `staging-prod-environment` memory), that flavor is currently the *only* distribution channel for beta testers too. Testers filling out feedback saw "1.6.0 (prod)", which reads as "this is the live release" when it's actually the beta.

**Fix applied:** `BetaFeedbackViewModel.kt` now hardcodes `flavor = "beta"` instead of reading `BuildConfig.FLAVOR`. This is safe specifically because the feedback screen is only reachable when `BuildConfig.IS_BETA_BUILD` is true (gated in `PersonalizeScreen.kt:171`) — anywhere this screen renders, it's a beta build by construction. The Help/About screen (`HelpScreen.kt:87`) still shows the real `BuildConfig.FLAVOR` and was deliberately left alone — that one is for debugging which backend you're actually hitting, and showing the true flavor there is correct.

**Files**
- `app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/feedback/presentation/BetaFeedbackViewModel.kt`

**Verification:** `./gradlew :app:compileProdDebugKotlin` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not run on-device (pure string literal change, no UI logic path affected).

## Item 2 — Records module won't stay compact at thousands of transactions

- **Status:** DONE `20a2482` — built, compiles green (`testStagingDebugUnitTest`: 582 tests, 0 failures, incl. 8 new in `MonthWindowTest`/`DayGroupingTest`; `assembleStagingDebug` also green), confirmed on-device by Alvin. See ADR-0032.
- **Severity:** Medium (not felt yet at current data volumes, but structurally unbounded — the query and the UI both scale linearly with total transaction count forever)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet for the month-window + grouping change (follows existing patterns); only reach for Paging3 if the month-window default turns out not to be enough

**Built as:** new `core/date/MonthWindow.kt` (month-snap/step math, pure Kotlin — `windowFor(anchor, zone)` returns `monthStart`/`startInclusive`/`endExclusive`, `step(monthStart, forward)`) and `core/date/DayGrouping.kt` (generic `groupByDay(items, dateOf, zone, today, isCurrentMonth)` producing sticky-header buckets labeled via `dayHeaderLabel` — "Today"/"Yesterday" only when `isCurrentMonth`, else a plain `"EEE, MMM d"` format pinned to `Locale.ENGLISH` for determinism). `AnalysisPeriodRange`'s MONTH branch now delegates to `MonthWindow` (existing `AnalysisPeriodRangeTest` unchanged, still green — pure extraction, no behavior change).

`TransactionDao` gained bounded overloads — `observeTransactions(userId, startInclusive, endExclusive)` and `observeCombined(startInclusive, endExclusive)` — plus `observeHasAnyTransaction(userId)`/`observeHasAnyCombinedTransaction()` (`SELECT EXISTS(...)`, cheap boolean signal for the empty-state distinction). The original unbounded `observeTransactions(userId)` stays (Analysis/Budgets/`BudgetAlertWorker` still need the full stream for their own windowing); the unbounded `observeCombined()` was removed outright since CombinedViewModel was the only caller and it's now fully month-windowed. `TransactionRepository`/`TransactionRepositoryImpl` and `ObserveTransactionsUseCase`/`ObserveCombinedTransactionsUseCase` mirror this (the former gained an overload, the latter's single method now takes a range); two new tiny use cases, `ObserveHasAnyTransactionUseCase`/`ObserveHasAnyCombinedTransactionUseCase`, wrap the boolean signal.

`TransactionsViewModel` and `CombinedViewModel` each hold their own `viewedMonth: MutableStateFlow<LocalDate>` (defaults to the current month, `flatMapLatest`-switched into the bounded query on step) — fully independent per decision 1, confirmed by construction (two separate ViewModel instances, no shared state). `CombinedViewModel`'s per-member monthly spend and couple-budget lookup now key off the *viewed* month instead of always "today" — a natural generalization once the window became steppable (previously there was no month-stepping concept in Combined at all), so paging Combined to a past/future month also pages its budget-editing target, symmetric with how Analysis already treats past-month budgets as read/writable via `yearMonth` lookup. New shared `core/ui/MonthStepperRow.kt` (label + prev/next arrows, same shape as Analysis's private `PeriodStepper`) is used by both `TransactionsScreen` and `CombinedScreen`, placed outside each screen's `PullToRefreshBox` so pulling the list doesn't fight the stepper.

Both screens' `LazyColumn`s now use Compose Foundation's `stickyHeader` (a `LazyListScope` member method in the installed BOM `2026.06.00` — no import needed, unlike older Foundation versions) to render day-grouped headers. Each screen's empty state now branches three ways: no account yet (Records only) → "no transactions/activity yet" (true zero, `!hasAnyTransactionEver`/`!hasAnySharedActivityEver`) → "no transactions/activity this month" (history exists elsewhere, `dayGroups` empty for the viewed month only).

**Note on Combined's has-any-ever edge case:** `observeHasAnyCombinedTransaction()` counts any shared row including `TRANSFER` type, but `CombinedLedgerCalculator.entries` excludes transfers — so a couple whose entire shared history is transfer-only would see "no shared activity this month" forever instead of the true-zero message. Judged an acceptable, self-correcting edge case (resolves the moment any expense/income is shared) rather than worth threading a type filter into the DAO query.

**Files touched:** new `core/date/MonthWindow.kt`, `core/date/DayGrouping.kt`, `core/ui/MonthStepperRow.kt`; `AnalysisPeriodRange.kt` (MONTH delegates to `MonthWindow`); `TransactionDao.kt`, `TransactionRepository.kt`, `TransactionRepositoryImpl.kt`, `ObserveTransactionsUseCase.kt`, `ObserveCombinedTransactionsUseCase.kt`, new `ObserveHasAnyTransactionUseCase.kt`/`ObserveHasAnyCombinedTransactionUseCase.kt`; `TransactionsUiState.kt`, `TransactionsViewModel.kt`, `TransactionsScreen.kt`; `CombinedUiState.kt`, `CombinedViewModel.kt`, `CombinedScreen.kt`. Test fakes updated for the new `TransactionRepository`/`TransactionDao` methods: `TransactionTestFixtures.kt` (`FakeTransactionDao`), `CoupleTestFixtures.kt` (`CountingTransactionRepo`), `SettlementUseCaseTest.kt`/`PaidOnBehalfUseCaseTest.kt` (`RecordingTransactionRepository`). New tests: `MonthWindowTest.kt`, `DayGroupingTest.kt`.

**Verify on-device (Alvin):** in Records, confirm the month stepper appears once an account exists, paging prev/next changes the visible transactions and day headers, "Today"/"Yesterday" only show when viewing the actual current month, and the two empty-state messages appear correctly (brand-new user vs. an existing user viewing an empty month). Repeat in Couple → Combined, plus confirm the couple budget card now follows whichever month is being viewed.

**What's wrong:** confirmed by reading the code, not just guessing:
- `TransactionDao.observeTransactions()` (`TransactionDao.kt:18-25`) has no `LIMIT`, no date filter — it's a `Flow` over the user's entire transaction history, forever. Room re-runs and re-emits the *whole* result set on every write to the table. `observeCombined()` (`TransactionDao.kt:34-41`, feeding `CombinedViewModel` in `feature/couple/presentation/`) has the identical problem — a second, separate screen with the same unbounded query.
- `TransactionsViewModel.uiState` (`TransactionsViewModel.kt:37-57`) re-maps the entire list (joining account/category names) on every emission.
- `TransactionsScreen.kt` renders one flat `LazyColumn` (`TransactionsScreen.kt:129-141`) of full-height cards (title + subtitle + date + amount, ~90dp each) — no date grouping, no filters, no search. `LazyColumn` itself only composes visible rows, so scroll *rendering* isn't the bottleneck; the cost is in the unbounded query + full-list re-map on every write, and the pure UX weight of scrolling a flat list with no landmarks.

**Decisions (locked in during the 2026-07-04 grilling session, see ADR-0032):**
1. **Scope: both Records (personal) and Combined view (couple)** get this fix — same architectural problem, two different ViewModels. Each screen tracks its own viewed month **independently** — no shared "current month" state between them.
2. **Default window: current calendar month** (e.g. all of July 1–31), stepped via prev/next arrows — calendar-aligned like Analysis's `MONTH` period (ADR-0030), not a trailing "last 30 days" window.
3. **Reuse Analysis's stepping math, but via a new shared `core/` utility, not a feature-to-feature import.** Extract the month-snap/step logic (`withDayOfMonth(1)` / `plusMonths(1)`) out of `AnalysisPeriodRange` into `core/date/MonthWindow.kt`; both `AnalysisPeriodRange` and the new Records/Combined code call that shared function. Matches CLAUDE.md's Scalability Principle (shared logic in `core/`, not buried in one feature). Worth a small unit test on the extracted date math per CLAUDE.md's testing policy.
4. **Sticky date-group headers by day, not month** — a month-level header would be redundant once the view is already bounded to one month. Day headers use relative labels ("Today"/"Yesterday") only when the viewed month is the actual current month; every other day (including other days within the current month, or any day when viewing a past/future month) gets a plain date format (e.g. "Wed, Jul 1").
5. **Empty state distinguishes "no transactions this month" vs. "no transactions ever."** The existing zero-state (`TransactionsScreen.kt:122-127`, "No transactions yet / Tap + to record...") stays reserved for a genuinely brand-new user; a user with history elsewhere but nothing in the viewed month gets a distinct "No transactions this month" message instead. Needs one extra has-any-transaction-ever signal threaded into the UI state.
6. **Search/filter bar** (account, category, type) confirmed **deferred** to a separate follow-on slice — genuinely new UI pattern (no existing `SearchBar`/filter component anywhere in the codebase to reuse), and bundling it would violate CLAUDE.md's "one concern per change." No placeholder icon reserved in the TopAppBar for it either — the future slice adds its own.
7. **Not recommended yet:** `Paging3`. It's the technically "correct" fix for true unbounded scale, but it's a bigger lift (new dependency, `PagingSource` on the DAO, `LazyPagingItems` in Compose) and the month-window default already bounds the common case. Revisit only if real usage shows the month window itself getting too large (e.g. a power user with hundreds of transactions in one month).

**Files likely touched:** `TransactionDao.kt` (add date-range query params to both `observeTransactions()` and `observeCombined()`), `TransactionRepositoryImpl.kt`, `ObserveTransactionsUseCase.kt`/`ObserveCombinedTransactionsUseCase.kt` (add a date-range parameter), `TransactionsViewModel.kt`, `CombinedViewModel.kt`, `TransactionsUiState.kt`, `TransactionsScreen.kt`, couple's combined-view screen, new `core/date/MonthWindow.kt` (extracted from `AnalysisPeriodRange.kt`, which is updated to call it).

**Tests to add:** the extracted `core/date/MonthWindow.kt` month-snap/step math — pure Kotlin, cheap, fits CLAUDE.md's testing bar for date math. The has-any-transaction-ever empty-state signal is worth a small test too if it lands in a UseCase/repository method rather than being derived inline in the ViewModel.

## Item 3 — Forgot password flow doesn't exist

- **Status:** DONE `b1688d6` — built per the decisions below, then hardened through live on-device + emulator debugging with Alvin that surfaced and fixed three real bugs beyond the original scope. See "What actually shipped" below.
- **Severity:** Medium-High (real, user-facing gap — CLAUDE.md's own nav map lists "Login → Register → Forgot password" as the auth graph, but only the first two exist)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet — the session-routing design is now settled (see decisions below), so the original Opus escalation no longer applies

**Current state, confirmed by reading the code:**
- `AuthScreen.kt` is a single screen that toggles between `SIGN_IN`/`SIGN_UP` mode. No "Forgot password?" link, no reset UI anywhere.
- `AuthRepository`/`AuthRepositoryImpl` has `signUp`, `signIn`, `signOut` only — no password-reset method, no corresponding `AuthError` case.
- The app already owns the deep-link plumbing this feature needs: `AndroidManifest.xml` registers an intent-filter for `com.iponlove.app://login-callback` (used today for the email-confirmation link), and `MainActivity.handleAuthDeepLink()` forwards the intent to `supabaseClient.handleDeeplinks(intent)`. That same mechanism is what Supabase's password-recovery email link would need to land on — this is a **reuse**, not a new deep-link system.

**The gotcha (why this isn't just "add a screen"):** supabase-kt's `SessionStatus.Authenticated` fires the same way whether the session came from a normal sign-in *or* from tapping a password-recovery email link. `AuthRepositoryImpl.status` (`AuthRepositoryImpl.kt:28-34`) maps `SessionStatus.Authenticated` straight to `AuthStatus.Authenticated(userId)`, and `MainActivity` routes `Authenticated` straight into the main app. So today, if we wired the recovery redirect to the existing deep link without anything else, tapping "reset my password" in the email would silently log the user into the app instead of prompting them to set a new password — a confusing (and arguably unsafe) dead end. This needs a distinct `AuthStatus.PasswordRecovery` (or similar) state, sourced from whatever `SessionSource`/recovery signal the current supabase-kt version exposes on `SessionStatus.Authenticated`, so `MainActivity` can route it to a "set new password" screen instead of the authenticated app shell.

**Decisions (locked in during the 2026-07-04 grilling session):**
1. **SDK gotcha resolved.** Decompiled the installed `io.github.jan-tennert.supabase` `auth-kt` 3.6.0 jar directly: `SessionStatus.Authenticated.session` (a `UserSession`) carries a `type: String` field — the raw `type` param from the recovery deep link's fragment (`"recovery"` for password-reset links). `AuthRepositoryImpl.kt:30` currently discards it. See ADR-0027 for the full fix.
2. **Entry point:** a `TextButton` under the sign-in button on `AuthScreen`, shown only in `SIGN_IN` mode. Confirmed with Alvin.
3. **Separate `ForgotPasswordScreen`**, not a third `AuthMode` on `AuthScreen` — the existing mode toggle is built around two credential-entry forms and doesn't fit a third, structurally different (email-only, terminal-success) flow. Reuse the *visual pattern* of `ConfirmationBanner` (generalized to take a `message: String`), not the literal composable (its copy is hardcoded to sign-up).
4. **New "set new password" screen**, reachable only via the recovery deep link + `AuthStatus.PasswordRecovery` gate. Has a **confirm-password field** (double entry) — a typo here costs a whole new recovery-email round trip, unlike sign-in. Alvin also asked to add confirm-password to the **sign-up** form for consistency — apply the same double-entry pattern there too.
5. **Post-reset routing:** force `client.auth.signOut()` after a successful password update, returning to ordinary `SIGN_IN` — never auto-continue the recovery session into the app. Matches the standard pattern (Gmail, banking apps) and avoids depending on unverified SDK behavior around whether `session.type` clears after `updateUser()`.
6. Out-of-code setup step (unchanged): the Supabase dashboard's password-reset email template needs its redirect URL pointed at the app's deep-link scheme — a dashboard config change for Alvin, not code. Flag explicitly when this ships.

**Files likely touched:** `AuthStatus.kt`, `AuthRepositoryImpl.kt`, `AuthRepository.kt` (add send-reset / update-password methods), `AuthError.kt` (new error cases), `AuthScreen.kt` (entry point + confirm-password field for sign-up), `ConfirmationBanner` (generalize to accept a `message: String`), new `ForgotPasswordScreen.kt` + `ResetPasswordScreen.kt` (confirm-password field), `AndroidManifest.xml` (extend or add a deep-link host), `MainActivity.kt` (routing + deep-link disambiguation).

**What actually shipped:** built as designed — `AuthStatus.PasswordRecovery(userId)` (checks `session.type == "recovery"` in `AuthRepositoryImpl.status`), new `SendPasswordResetUseCase`/`UpdatePasswordUseCase`, new `ForgotPasswordScreen`/`ForgotPasswordViewModel`/`ForgotPasswordUiState` and `ResetPasswordScreen`/`ResetPasswordViewModel`/`ResetPasswordUiState`, confirm-password field added to both sign-up (`AuthScreen`) and the new reset screen, `MainActivity` routes `PasswordRecovery` to `ResetPasswordScreen` and toggles `Unauthenticated` between `AuthScreen`/`ForgotPasswordScreen` via local state (no Navigation-Compose in the auth gate, matching the existing convention). `AndroidManifest.xml` needed no change — the existing `login-callback` intent-filter already covers both flows.

**Three real bugs found and fixed via live emulator/on-device debugging (not part of the original design, surfaced only once Alvin tried the actual email round-trip):**
1. **The `Auth` plugin was never configured with `scheme`/`host`** (`SupabaseClient.kt`, `install(Auth) { }` was empty). Decompiled `auth-kt` 3.6.0's `handleDeeplinks()` bytecode directly: it compares the incoming URI's scheme/host against `AuthConfig.scheme`/`.host` and **silently returns** on any mismatch — before ever touching the fragment. Since both default to `null`, **every** deep link (recovery, and technically email-confirmation too) was being dropped with zero trace, no exception, no log. Fixed by setting `scheme = "com.iponlove.app"` / `host = "login-callback"` in `install(Auth) { }`. This was the actual root cause of "tapping the email link does nothing," confirmed by replaying a captured real recovery fragment through the fixed build and seeing `handleDeeplinks: session established, type=recovery` fire, landing on "Set a new password."
2. **`AuthErrorClassifier` didn't recognize GoTrue's real weak-password message.** This project's Supabase Auth settings enforce a character-class password policy (upper+lower+digit+symbol), not just length. Its rejection message ends in the raw error code `weak_password` (underscore) and includes the phrase "password should contain" — neither matched the classifier's old `"weak password"` (space) check, so it fell through to generic "Something went wrong." Also strengthened `AuthCredentials.validatePassword` client-side to check the same character classes, avoiding an avoidable round-trip for the same rejection.
3. **GoTrue already rejects a recovery password change that matches the account's current password** (error code `same_password`, confirmed via `AuthErrorCode.SamePassword` in the decompiled SDK) — this needed no new validation logic, just classifying the existing server rejection instead of letting it fall through to "Something went wrong."

**Also added (post-build refinements from Alvin's testing):** reveal/hide password toggle (eye icon) on both fields of `ResetPasswordScreen`; a "Back to sign in" option on that same screen (`ResetPasswordViewModel.cancel()`, signs out of the recovery session without changing the password — there was previously no way out of that screen if the user changed their mind).

**Files touched (final):** all originally-listed files above, plus `SupabaseClient.kt` (`Auth` scheme/host config — the actual root-cause fix), `AuthErrorClassifier.kt` (weak_password/same_password/rate-limit message matching), `AuthCredentials.kt` (character-class password validation + `validatePasswordsMatch`), `SignUpUseCase.kt` (confirm-password param). New tests: `AuthCredentialsTest` (password character-class + match cases), `AuthErrorClassifierTest` (weak_password character-class message, same_password, rate-limit).

**Still needed before this ships to real testers:** the Supabase dashboard's password-reset email template redirect URL and the Redirect URLs allow-list both need `com.iponlove.app://login-callback` — Alvin confirmed this is already configured on the staging project during this session's testing.

## Item 4 — Navbar editor: "Couple" shows pinned + "Paired only" while unpaired, then vanishes entirely after being replaced

- **Status:** DONE `8fe6c83` — grew well beyond the originally scoped "More modules" filter tweak once on-device testing (Alvin, 2026-07-04) surfaced that the underlying ADR-0017 pairing-gate design let the bar and the editor disagree about what was pinned at all, not just about Couple's caption. See "What actually shipped" below for the final design and two data-isolation bugs found and fixed along the way.
- **Severity:** Low-Medium (confusing UX, not data loss — recoverable by re-pairing — but reads as a real bug in the moment)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low (small, contained change)

**Important correction first:** this is a *different* issue from the fixed-pin-count redesign described in the `navbar-fixed-pin-count-plan` memory. That memory said "not started" but it actually **shipped** in `b2c250e` ("navbar always shows exactly 3 pins; fold in F7 + F11 fixes") — confirmed via `git log` and `docs/build/v1.5-post-ship-audit.md` F7/F8, both marked `DONE b2c250e`. The memory file is stale and is being corrected alongside this doc. The bug reported here exists *within* that already-shipped design, not because the redesign is missing.

**Part A — why "Couple" appears "On the bar" tagged "Paired only" while unpaired:** this part is working as designed, not a bug, but the wording is confusing. `NavbarEditorScreen.kt`'s "On the bar" list renders directly from `NavConfig.pinnedIds` — the user's stored layout *intent* — not from what's actually rendering on the physical bottom bar. This is deliberate (ADR-0017's 2026-07-03 addendum): config outlives unpairing so re-pairing instantly restores the exact previous layout, instead of the user having to manually re-pin Couple every time they pair/unpair. Since the default pins are Analysis/Records/Couple, an unpaired user who never customized their bar sees "Couple" in "On the bar" tagged "Paired only" — while the real bar (via `NavResolver.visiblePinIds`, `NavResolver.kt:26-54`) is showing Manage back-filled into that slot. The section is technically named for "what you've chosen," not "what's currently rendering," and that distinction isn't visible in the UI at all — worth a copy/label tweak even if the underlying model doesn't change (e.g. a one-line hint under the section header when a paired-only pin is present and unavailable).

**Part B — the real inconsistency, why Couple "disappears":** `NavbarEditorScreen.kt:76-78`'s "More modules" list filters out any `requiresPaired` destination while unpaired:
```kotlin
val available = NavRegistry.all.filter {
    it.pinnable && it.id !in config.pinnedIds && (!it.requiresPaired || isPaired)
}
```
But the "On the bar" list applies no such filter to an already-pinned paired-only module — it's always shown, just tagged. So the two lists treat the exact same condition (`requiresPaired && !isPaired`) inconsistently depending on whether the module happens to currently occupy a pin slot. The moment a user replaces Couple out of the pin set (e.g. swapping it for Manage) while unpaired, Couple satisfies neither list's filter and vanishes from the editor entirely — not on the bar, not in "More modules." Nothing is corrupted (`NavConfig.replace()` just no longer references `"couple"` anywhere), but there's no way to get it back from the editor until re-pairing makes it reappear in "More modules." That dead end is what reads as a bug.

**Fix direction (proposed, not yet built):** drop the `(!it.requiresPaired || isPaired)` clause from the "More modules" filter so paired-only destinations always show there too, tagged "Paired only" the same way pinned rows already are. This makes the two lists consistent — a paired-only module is now always visible *somewhere* in the editor, never fully hidden. It's a small, contained change to one filter expression in `NavbarEditorScreen.kt`. The underlying data model already supports this: `NavConfig.replace()` (`NavConfig.kt:20-28`) only checks `pinnable`, not pairing state, so swapping a paired-only module *into* a pin slot while unpaired already works today — this fix just makes that capability visible/reachable via "More modules" instead of only reachable by having it already pinned.

**Decision (2026-07-04):** with paired-only modules now always visible in "More modules," tapping one while unpaired still works exactly like today — it stores the intent via `replace()`, it just won't render on the real bar until paired. The row stays interactive, not disabled, consistent with "config is intent, not current state," which is the whole point of the addendum.

**Files:** `app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavbarEditorScreen.kt` (the `available` filter, line ~76-78).

**Tests to add:** none needed for a filter-expression change on a Composable (per CLAUDE.md, UI isn't unit-tested pre-stabilization) — verify by running on-device: unpair, replace Couple out of the pin set, confirm "Couple" now appears tagged "Paired only" in "More modules" instead of disappearing.

**What actually shipped (2026-07-04, `8fe6c83`):** the small filter fix above was applied first and looked correct in isolation, but Alvin's on-device retest (brand-new user `testdev9`) showed the bar rendering **Manage** while the editor's "On the bar" list showed **Couple** — the two had never actually been guaranteed to agree, because the old `NavResolver` gated Couple off the *bar* by pairing state while the editor read the raw stored `NavConfig` unfiltered. That's a structurally different bug than the filter-expression fix addressed, so the design was reworked instead of patched further:

- **Pairing state no longer filters or rewrites the bar at all.** `NavResolver.visiblePinIds` now returns `NavConfig.pinnedIds` (known/pinnable ids only, back-filled if short) with no pairing check — the bar, "On the bar", and the saved config are always the same three ids by construction. `requiresPaired` on `NavDestination` is now informational-only (drives the editor's "Paired only" caption, nothing else).
- **Couple's screen handles unpaired itself.** `CoupleScreen` now renders the same create/join pairing body (`CoupleOverviewBody`) that Settings → Couple uses whenever the user isn't fully paired, and only shows the Combined/Debts tabs once paired — so pinning Couple while unpaired opens pairing instead of a dead tab.
- **New solo default:** `NavRegistry.DEFAULT_PINS` changed from `[analysis, records, couple]` to `[analysis, records, manage]` — a fresh install no longer defaults to a paired-only pin it can't use yet.
- **Pin-on-create/join, not auto-append:** a new `PinCoupleShortcutUseCase` explicitly pins Couple (swapping out Manage, or the last pin) right after `CoupleViewModel.createCouple()`/`redeemInvite()` succeeds — the one deliberate, user-initiated config write tied to pairing. Passive pairing changes (partner redeems your code, unpair) never touch the layout, per Alvin's explicit instruction not to auto-append Couple on incidental pairing.
- Confirmed good on-device by Alvin for the solo case (fresh install, Manage on the bar, Couple correctly in "More modules" tagged "Paired only") after a clean uninstall/reinstall to clear the old stored config.

**Two data-isolation bugs found and fixed in the same pass** (surfaced while testing account-switching on-device, unrelated to the navbar mechanism itself but fixed here since they blocked verifying it cleanly):
1. **`LocalDataWiper` never cleared the local app-lock PIN.** Signing into a different account left the previous user's PIN in place, so the new account could get locked out behind a code it never set. Fixed by adding `appLock.clearPin()` to `LocalDataWiper.wipe()` — covers both the clean sign-out path (`AuthViewModel.signOut()`) and the defensive account-switch-guard path (`AccountSwitchGuard`) since both funnel through the same wiper.
2. **Root cause of why the PIN survived even a full uninstall+reinstall: `android:allowBackup="true"`.** Android's Auto Backup was silently restoring the app's entire private storage (DataStore prefs including the PIN, Room cache) from the signed-in Google account during install — *before* the app's own account-switch wipe logic ever got to run. Fixed by setting `allowBackup="false"` in `AndroidManifest.xml`; Supabase is already the source of truth, so nothing local needs to survive a reinstall. This closes a real gap beyond just the PIN — the same mechanism could have restored stale Room data across a reinstall/device-transfer for any real user, not just test accounts.

**Files touched (final):** `NavDestination.kt` (`DEFAULT_PINS`, `requiresPaired` doc), `NavResolver.kt` (rewritten, pairing-agnostic), `NavConfig.kt` (new `ensurePinned()`), `NavbarViewModel.kt`/`NavUiState` (adapted), `NavbarEditorScreen.kt` (the original filter fix + "Paired only" caption on `AvailableRow`), `CoupleScreen.kt` (renders pairing body when not fully paired), `CoupleViewModel.kt` (calls `PinCoupleShortcutUseCase` on create/join), new `PinCoupleShortcutUseCase.kt`, `LocalDataWiper.kt` (+PIN clear), `AndroidManifest.xml` (`allowBackup=false`). Tests: `NavResolverTest.kt` rewritten for pairing-agnostic semantics, `NavConfigTest.kt` gained `ensurePinned` cases, `LocalDataWiperTest.kt` gained a PIN-clear assertion.

## Item 6 — "Use biometric" doesn't work when the app gets locked

- **Status:** DONE `c59111c` — confirmed working on-device by Alvin (Nothing Phone 2a) 2026-07-05, both cold and after a timeout-lock cycle, verified via `adb logcat` showing `launching biometric prompt` actually firing (previously silent). Scope per Alvin's explicit instruction: biometric must auto-prompt first on every lock/timeout, PIN is backup only.

**Actual root cause (2026-07-05, found via on-device Logcat repro — the earlier bytecode-only mechanisms below were real bugs and are still fixed, but were not what Alvin was hitting):** `LockScreen.kt`'s `launchBiometric()` used `context as? FragmentActivity` to get the Activity for `BiometricPrompt`. But this screen renders inside a `Dialog(...)` composable, and the actually-resolved `androidx.compose.ui:ui-android:1.11.3` (confirmed via `dependencies` — not the `1.7.5` the original 2026-07-04 grilling session happened to check) wraps that Dialog's context in a `ContextThemeWrapper` before constructing it (decompiled `DialogWrapper.<init>`: `new ContextThemeWrapper(composeView.context, themeResId)`, passed straight to `ComponentDialog`'s constructor). `LocalContext.current` inside the lock screen is therefore that wrapper, not `MainActivity` — and a direct `as?` cast on a `ContextWrapper` returns `null` silently, no exception, no log. `launchBiometric()` silently no-opped to the PIN pad on **every single call**, which is why "Use biometric" appeared to do nothing and timeout always landed on PIN. Fixed with a standard `Context.findActivity()` tailrec unwrap of the `ContextWrapper` chain instead of a direct cast. This was the actual bug the whole time; item 6's original "ruled out by static analysis" conclusion (candidate 4) was checking a stale dependency version.

**Three additional real (but secondary) issues found via `androidx.biometric:1.1.0` bytecode analysis while investigating — kept fixed since they're still live bugs, just not the one Alvin was hitting:**
1. **The timeout-lock auto-prompt could be silently dropped.** The 30s auto-lock (`AppLockManager.scheduleAutoLock`) flips `isLocked` while the app is *backgrounded* (scheduled from `onStop`), so the lock `Dialog` can mount — and a one-shot launch fire — after `onSaveInstanceState()`, where `BiometricPrompt.authenticateInternal`'s `fragmentManager.isStateSaved()` guard silently returns. Fixed by making the auto-prompt focus-gated and re-arming (`snapshotFlow { LocalWindowInfo.isWindowFocused }`) instead of a mount-time one-shot — a focused window can't be state-saved, and it self-heals any swallowed cancel.
2. **A stuck `isPromptShowing` flag could make later attempts no-op.** `BiometricFragment.showPromptForAuthentication()` opens with `if (mViewModel.isPromptShowing()) return;` — silent — and the flag lives in an Activity-scoped `BiometricViewModel` that survives lock cycles; on API 29+ the library's own `onStop()` does nothing, so a skipped dismissal callback (OEM background/focus-change cancels) leaves it stuck until Activity recreation. Fixed with a reflective `clearStuckBiometricPromptFlag()` guard before every launch, safe because it only runs from a focused lock window (a true flag in that state is provably stale).
3. **`ERROR_CANCELED` (system-initiated cancel, e.g. a keyguard-transition race holding the under-display sensor) was being treated as a deliberate dismissal**, silently dropping to PIN instead of retrying — this was the ~0.1s prompt-flash-then-PIN Alvin saw mid-session before the real cast bug was found. Fixed with a 500ms-delayed retry bounded by a shared attempt cap; only genuinely user-initiated codes (negative button, user cancel) stay terminal-to-pad.

All four fixes ship together in this one commit-pending change — the cast fix alone was sufficient to resolve Alvin's reported symptom, but the other three are real, independently-verified bugs in the same code path and are cheap to carry (see "Files touched").

**The earlier lead was a red herring:** `androidx.biometric`'s own manifest merges `USE_BIOMETRIC` + `USE_FINGERPRINT` into every APK — confirmed in `app/build/intermediates/merged_manifests/` from builds predating any manifest edit. The permission was never actually missing at install time (consistent with biometric having worked occasionally). The explicit `<uses-permission>` line now in `AndroidManifest.xml` is kept as harmless documentation.

**Fix (all in `LockScreen.kt`, plus one ProGuard rule):**
- **Focus-gated, re-arming auto-prompt** replaces the mount-time one-shot: `snapshotFlow { LocalWindowInfo.isWindowFocused }` launches the prompt whenever the lock window gains focus while still in biometric mode. A focused window is never state-saved (kills mechanism 1), and re-arming on focus regain self-heals OEM no-callback cancels. No cancel→prompt→cancel loop: every callback-delivered non-success flips `showPinPad`, which stops the re-arm; `MAX_AUTO_PROMPT_ATTEMPTS = 3` bounds the no-callback case.
- **Stuck-flag clearer:** `clearStuckBiometricPromptFlag()` runs before every launch — reflectively reads `BiometricViewModel.isPromptShowing` and resets it if true (kills mechanism 2). Safe by construction: it's only ever called from a focused lock window, and if our window has focus no system prompt can actually be up, so a true flag is provably stale. Reflection failure is caught and non-fatal. New ProGuard keep for `androidx.biometric.BiometricViewModel` in `proguard-rules.pro` (release builds minify).
- **Errors surfaced:** lockout keeps its item-8 message; deliberate dismissals (negative button / user cancel / system cancel) stay silent; every other error now shows "Biometric unavailable: <OS error string>" under the pad (`biometricLockoutMessage` generalized to `biometricMessage`). All launch attempts and error codes are logged under tag `LockScreen` for any future Logcat repro.

**Verify on-device (Alvin):** enable biometric, background the app >30s, reopen → the system prompt should appear automatically (PIN pad only after cancel/failure). Repeat several cycles, including: cancel the prompt then re-lock; background the app *while the prompt is showing* then return (the historical stuck-flag trigger); force-stop + cold start.

**On-device debugging session, 2026-07-05, Nothing Phone 2a (this is what actually found and confirmed the real bug):**
1. **First round:** the fix above (auto-prompt + stuck-flag clearer + error surfacing) still went straight to PIN — no visible change. Live Logcat via `adb -s <serial> logcat -s "LockScreen:*"` showed `auto-launching biometric prompt (attempt 1)` firing but **nothing after it** — not even the `launching biometric prompt` line one call deeper, and not the reflective clearer's failure log either. That gap (silence between two adjacent log lines with no exception) pointed at the one un-logged branch in between: the `context as? FragmentActivity` cast.
2. **Confirmed the resolved compose-ui version:** `./gradlew app:dependencies` showed `androidx.compose.ui:ui-android:1.11.3` actually resolves for this build — not the `1.7.5` the original 2026-07-04 grilling session happened to check.
3. **Decompiled 1.11.3's `DialogWrapper` directly:** its constructor does `new ContextThemeWrapper(composeView.getContext(), themeResId)` and passes that wrapper straight into `ComponentDialog`'s super-constructor. So `LocalContext.current` inside the lock `Dialog`'s content (this screen) is a `ContextThemeWrapper`, not `MainActivity` — and `context as? FragmentActivity` on a `ContextWrapper` returns `null` silently, no exception, no log. This is the actual root cause; item 6's original "ruled out by static analysis" call (candidate 4) was correct for 1.7.5 but wrong for the version actually in use.
4. **Fixed** with a `Context.findActivity()` tailrec unwrap of the `ContextWrapper` chain, replacing the direct cast. Rebuilt, reinstalled, retested with fresh Logcat: `launching biometric prompt` now fires immediately after `auto-launching`, across two separate lock cycles — **confirmed working by Alvin on-device.**
5. A ~0.1s fingerprint-flash-then-PIN was also observed mid-session (before the cast fix), diagnosed as the system killing the prompt with `ERROR_CANCELED` right after keyguard dismissal (sensor still held by the lock-screen transition) — the retry-on-`ERROR_CANCELED` fix (see below) addresses this and remains in place as a real, independently-useful hardening even though the cast bug turned out to be the primary blocker.

If anything ever regresses, `adb -s <serial> logcat -s "LockScreen:*" "BiometricPromptCompat:*" "BiometricFragment:*"` captures the exact path (quote the filter args — zsh globs unquoted `Tag:*`).

<details><summary>Pre-fix investigation record (2026-07-04, superseded)</summary>
- **Severity:** Medium-High (breaks the primary unlock path for anyone who's enabled biometric — they fall through to PIN every time, which defeats the point of turning it on)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet to reproduce + fix once the trigger is confirmed
- **Reported by Alvin, might be the same root cause as Item 7 — investigate together, not separately.**

**Symptom, confirmed with Alvin directly (not guessed):** on his real device (not the emulator), the system biometric prompt showed successfully "5/100 times" historically but now fails every single lock cycle, with no cold-start-vs-warm distinction. Critically, tapping the manual "Use biometric" fallback button (`LockScreen.kt:121`, an unconditional call to `launchBiometric()` with no dependency on any remembered state) also does **nothing visible** — no prompt, no error, no crash.

**Four candidate mechanisms checked this session — three ruled out, one open:**
1. ~~`collectAsState(initial=...)` race~~ — **ruled out.** This was the original doc's plausible mechanism (`appLockPrefs` defaulting `isBiometricEnabled=false` before the DataStore flow's first emission, on a cold-start race). Ruled out because Alvin confirmed the failure happens on *every* lock, not just after a cold start.
2. ~~Emulator has no enrolled/simulated fingerprint~~ — **ruled out.** Alvin is testing on his real device, which already has biometrics enrolled and has authenticated into Ipon successfully before.
3. ~~OS-level biometric lockout (`ERROR_LOCKOUT`/`ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT`, requiring a device-credential unlock to clear)~~ — **ruled out.** Alvin unlocked his phone's actual lock screen with PIN/pattern (clears any OS lockout) and retried; "Use biometric" still did nothing.
4. ~~`context as? FragmentActivity` cast failing because the lock `Dialog` wraps context differently~~ — **ruled out by static analysis, not on-device.** Decompiled the installed `androidx.compose.ui:ui-android:1.7.5` AAR: `DialogWrapper.setContent(CompositionContext, content)` takes a `CompositionContext` from the parent composition, meaning the Dialog's content sub-composition inherits `LocalContext` from `MainActivity`'s own composition rather than a separately-wrapped context. `MainActivity : FragmentActivity()` (confirmed, `MainActivity.kt:67`), so the cast at `LockScreen.kt:57` should succeed. This is inference from bytecode, not a Logcat-confirmed fact — treat as "very likely ruled out," not certain.

**Lead candidate, unconfirmed — missing manifest permission:** `AndroidManifest.xml` declares **neither** `android.permission.USE_BIOMETRIC` **nor** `android.permission.USE_FINGERPRINT` (grepped the full manifest, zero hits). The installed `androidx.biometric:biometric:1.1.0` (`gradle/libs.versions.toml:28`, `app/build.gradle.kts:152-153`) documents one of these two permissions as required for `BiometricPrompt`/`BiometricManager` to function — omitting it can cause `authenticate()` to fail immediately with no visible prompt on devices/OS versions that enforce the check strictly, which matches "nothing happens" exactly. This is a **confirmed gap** (the permission really is missing) but an **unconfirmed root cause** (not yet tested whether adding it fixes the symptom) — Alvin asked to record this as the lead candidate rather than apply it blind this session.

**Recommended next step when this item is picked up:** add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_BIOMETRIC" />` to `AndroidManifest.xml`, rebuild, install on Alvin's real device, and retest "Use biometric." If it starts working, done — that was the root cause. If not, the next diagnostic step is Logcat during a live repro (`adb logcat` while tapping "Use biometric") to see whether `onAuthenticationError`/`onAuthenticationFailed` fire at all, since all four static-analysis candidates are now exhausted.

</details>

**Files touched (final):** `app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/applock/presentation/LockScreen.kt` (the `Context.findActivity()` fix — the actual root-cause fix; plus focus-gated re-arming auto-prompt, stuck-flag clearer, `ERROR_CANCELED` retry, error surfacing, logging), `app/proguard-rules.pro` (keep rule for reflection), `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (explicit `USE_BIOMETRIC`, documentation-only — already merged by the library).

**Tests to add:** none — the fix is Compose/lifecycle/reflection glue with no pure-logic layer to extract; verify by running per CLAUDE.md's UI testing policy.

## Item 8 — No limit on wrong PIN/biometric attempts

- **Status:** DONE `a5b12d2`

**Built as:** new `domain/model/PinLockoutPolicy.kt` — pure object holding the flat 5-attempt/30-second-cooldown math (`onFailure`/`onSuccess`/`isLockedOut`/`remainingLockoutSeconds`), unit-tested directly with no DataStore/Android dependency. New `domain/model/PinVerifyResult.kt` sealed type (`Success`/`Failed(remainingAttempts)`/`LockedOut(remainingSeconds)`) replaces `VerifyPinUseCase`'s old `Boolean` return. `AppLockPreferences` gained `failedPinAttempts`/`pinLockoutUntil` fields (persisted in DataStore via `AppLockRepositoryImpl`, new `setPinAttemptState()` repo method); both `setPin()` and `clearPin()` now also reset the attempt/lockout state, so setting a fresh PIN never inherits stale lockout. `VerifyPinUseCase` now checks the persisted lockout before touching the PIN at all, and applies `PinLockoutPolicy` on failure/success — the counter never resets on elapsed time per the locked-in decision, only on a successful unlock. `AppLockViewModel.verify()` handles all three result branches, surfaces a "Too many attempts. Try again in Ns." message, and auto re-enables the pad via a delayed coroutine once the cooldown elapses (no live ticking countdown — out of scope for this effort level). `LockScreen.kt`'s numpad now no-ops while locked out. Biometric's OS-level `ERROR_LOCKOUT`/`ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT` codes now surface "Biometric temporarily locked out — use your PIN" instead of silently falling back to the PIN pad, per decision 4.

**Note on Hilt:** `VerifyPinUseCase`'s clock is *not* a constructor parameter — Dagger/Hilt ignores Kotlin default parameter values and would otherwise demand a binding for `() -> Instant`. It's an `internal var now` property instead, matching the constraint (not the `SyncClock`-style `@Provides` pattern, since this didn't warrant a new DI module for one test seam).
- **Severity:** Medium (security hardening, not a live exploit given this is a local-only PIN gating an already-authenticated Supabase session — but a real gap against the "PH fintech pattern" bar this app already holds itself to for Forgot PIN)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low-med (self-contained: a counter + a cooldown, no cross-ADR interaction)

**What's confirmed by reading the code:** there is **no attempt-limiting mechanism at all** for the PIN path — grepped the whole `feature/applock/` tree for attempt/lockout/fail-count fields and found none. `AppLockViewModel.verify()` (`AppLockViewModel.kt:46-55`) checks the PIN and on failure just sets `error = "Incorrect PIN"` — the user can retry immediately, indefinitely, with no backoff, no counter, no lockout. Contrast with **biometric**, which already gets OS-level lockout for free: Android's `BiometricPrompt` itself throws `ERROR_LOCKOUT` after repeated failures (and `ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT` after enough of those), and `LockScreen.kt:226-228`'s `onAuthenticationError` already routes every error code — lockout included — to the PIN pad. So biometric is already at "industry standard" via the OS; **PIN is the actual gap.**

**Context this app already has:** a PIN reset path exists and requires re-authenticating with the Supabase email+password (`ForgotPinDialog`, `ResetPinAfterReAuthUseCase`) — so a lockout doesn't need to design a recovery path from scratch, it already exists. This makes a lockout lower-risk to add: worst case of a bug in the lockout logic is "user re-verifies via email+password," not "user is permanently locked out."

**Decisions (locked in during the 2026-07-04 grilling session, see ADR-0028):**
1. **Flat 5-attempt threshold, not progressive.** This PIN only gates local access to an already-authenticated session, not a payment — progressive backoff's extra complexity isn't earning its keep here.
2. **30-second timed cooldown**, not forcing the "Forgot PIN" re-auth flow after N failures — a timer over-punishes an honest typo less than forcing email+password re-auth would.
3. **Counter persists in DataStore** (survives process death — force-killing the app cannot bypass the lockout) and **resets only on a successful unlock**, never on elapsed idle time (resetting on elapsed time would let a brute-forcer simply wait out the window).
4. **Scope: PIN gets the new lockout; biometric's existing OS-level lockout codes (`ERROR_LOCKOUT`/`ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT`) are now surfaced with a message** ("Biometric temporarily locked out — use your PIN") instead of silently falling back to the PIN pad. "Forgot PIN" remains available throughout as an opt-in escape hatch.

**Files likely touched:** `app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/applock/presentation/AppLockViewModel.kt` (`verify()`), `app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/applock/domain/model/AppLockPreferences.kt` (new counter/lockout-until fields, or a new small domain model), `AppLockRepository`/`AppLockRepositoryImpl` (persistence), `LockScreen.kt` (surfacing the cooldown state + optional biometric-lockout messaging).

**Tests to add:** yes — this is pure logic once the policy is set (attempt counting, threshold crossing, cooldown expiry), a good fit for a `VerifyPinUseCase`-level unit test per CLAUDE.md's testing policy (money/sync-adjacent correctness logic, cheap and JVM-only).

## Item 9 — Force beta testers to update on version mismatch

- **Status:** DONE `5aafe7a` — built, compiles green (`assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` both pass), confirmed on-device by Alvin. See ADR-0029 and the `Version-mismatch gate` glossary term in `CONTEXT.md`.

**Built as:** new `feature/appupdate/` folder — `domain/repository/AppReleaseInfoRepository.kt` (interface), `data/AppReleaseInfoRepositoryImpl.kt` (plain Postgrest `select().decodeSingle()`, no TableSyncer), `data/remote/AppReleaseInfoDto.kt`, `domain/usecase/CheckAppVersionUseCase.kt` (fail-open fetch + a pure `isMismatched(installed, required)` companion function, unit-tested), `presentation/AppVersionGateManager.kt` (singleton `StateFlow<Boolean>`, mirrors `AppLockManager`'s shape), `di/AppUpdateModule.kt`. `MainActivity.kt`: the existing `onStart` lifecycle observer now also calls `appVersionGateManager.check(BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE)` in its own coroutine (gated `IS_BETA_BUILD`, so it also runs pre-login since the observer is unconditional); a new blocking `Dialog` (`UpdateRequiredScreen`, "Update" → Play Store web URL) is declared *after* the existing `when(status)` block so its Window stacks above even the AppLock lock screen. Schema: `app_release_info` table appended to `supabase/schema.sql` + a new idempotent migration `supabase/migrations/2026-07-04_app_release_info.sql`, seeded to `required_version_code = 2` (matches the currently-shipped versionCode, so existing testers aren't blocked until Alvin bumps it for the next release).

**Fixed in passing:** `ShouldShowOnboardingUseCaseTest.kt`'s fake `OnboardingRepository` was missing an override for `reset()` (an interface method that already existed, unrelated to this item) — this broke compilation of the *entire* JVM test source set, so nothing could be run until it was patched. One-line stub fix, not otherwise related to Item 9.

**Still needed before this can ship:** the migration must be applied on the live staging Supabase project (SQL Editor) before the on-device test can see anything other than a fetch failure (which fails open — Alvin would just see no dialog rather than a broken one, so this is safe to test incrementally).
- **Severity:** N/A (beta-testing tooling, not a bug) — but high value: every other item in this doc gets tested more reliably if Alvin can guarantee testers are on the build he actually shipped
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low-med (the code itself follows existing patterns — a blocking `Dialog` like AppLock's, a simple Supabase read like `BetaFeedbackConfig`)

**What Alvin wants:** whenever a beta tester opens the app and their installed version doesn't match the latest version Alvin has released, force an update prompt before they can use the app. Beta only.

**Current state, confirmed by reading the code:** nothing like this exists today. `versionCode = 2` (`app/build.gradle.kts:28`, in `defaultConfig` — shared across both flavors, not per-flavor) is the only version signal in the app. There's no Supabase table, no remote-config mechanism, no version-check anywhere — this needs to be built from scratch, not wired into something existing.

**Decisions (locked in):**
1. **Where "latest version" lives:** one new Supabase table (e.g. `app_release_info`), single row, public-read RLS, no client write — Alvin updates the row manually each time he ships a new build. Needs a migration. Given decision 2 below, name the column `required_version_code`, not `min_version_code` — "min" implies floor semantics, which this isn't.
2. **Exact-match, not floor.** Alvin's actual goal is uniformity — every tester on the identical build, so bug reports are comparable — not merely "not behind." This means Alvin must bump the Supabase row on his own device *before* a new build reaches testers, or he'd force-block himself too.
3. **Hard, non-dismissable block** — no back-press, no close button, same shape as the existing `AppLock` lock `Dialog` (`MainActivity.kt:201-211`), but gating the whole app rather than resuming from background.
4. **"Update" opens `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iponlove.app`** — not `market://`, and not the internal-testing opt-in link. The web URL degrades gracefully via a browser if the Play Store app isn't installed; the opt-in link isn't needed since anyone who could see this dialog is, by construction, already enrolled (they have the app installed).
5. **Check cadence:** same foreground/resume lifecycle plumbing `AppLock` already uses in `MainActivity.kt` — not a second mechanism, not cold-launch-only.
6. **Network failure fails open** — a failed version-check call (offline, Supabase down) must never block the app; this isn't core functionality and blocking on it would violate the offline-first principle.

**Files likely touched:** new Supabase migration (`app_release_info` table + RLS), a small remote-read source/repository (a plain singleton read, not a synced entity — should NOT go through the full `TableSyncer`/push-pull machinery per ADR-0009, since there's nothing to push and no per-row sync semantics here), `MainActivity.kt` (new blocking `Dialog` gated by `BuildConfig.IS_BETA_BUILD`, alongside the existing lock `Dialog`), possibly a small new `feature/appupdate/` folder or folded into an existing small feature area.

**Tests to add:** the version-comparison logic itself (`installedVersionCode == requiredVersionCode`) is pure and cheap — worth a small unit test per CLAUDE.md's testing policy. The Supabase fetch and the blocking `Dialog` are UI/network glue — verify by running per CLAUDE.md's UI testing policy.

## Item 11 — Redesign Analysis time-range filter as crypto-app-style presets (1D/1W/1M/3M/6M/12M/ALL TIME)

- **Status:** DONE `d212361` — built, compiles green (`assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` both pass, 13 tests in `AnalysisPeriodRangeTest` incl. 6 new for the added periods), awaiting Alvin's on-device test. See ADR-0030 and the `Analysis period` glossary term in `CONTEXT.md`.
- **Severity:** N/A (UX enhancement)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low-med

**Built as:** `AnalysisPeriod` gained `QUARTER, SEMI_ANNUAL, ANNUAL, ALL_TIME` alongside `DAY, WEEK, MONTH`. `AnalysisPeriodRange.windowFor`/`.step` extended per-period: quarters snap to Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct 1 and span 3 months, halves snap to Jan/Jul 1 and span 6 months, years snap to Jan 1 and span 12 months — all steppable via the same `PeriodStepper` mechanism per ADR-0030. `ALL_TIME` is the one exception: `windowFor` ignores the anchor entirely and always returns a fixed window (`startInclusive` = 2000-01-01, `endExclusive` = `Instant.MAX`), and `step()` is a no-op for it since there's nothing to page to. `AnalysisViewModel.labelFor` formats the new buckets ("Q3 2026", "H1 2026", "2026", "All Time"). `AnalysisScreen`'s `PeriodSelector` was redesigned from an `IponFilterChip` row (which only comfortably fit ~3 chips) to a Material3 `ScrollableTabRow` with short labels (1D/1W/1M/3M/6M/12M/ALL), inherently horizontally-scrollable so all 7 options fit without wrapping. `PeriodStepper`'s prev/next `IconButton`s now take a `canStep` flag, disabled when the selected period is `ALL_TIME`. `MonthTabLayout` (Donut/Flow/Calendar tabs) is unchanged — it's still gated to `MONTH` only; the new periods fall through to the existing donut-only branch alongside Day/Week, since Flow/Calendar are month-shaped (`daysInMonth`-based) and were never in scope for the new buckets.

**Current state, confirmed by reading the code:** `AnalysisPeriod` is `DAY, WEEK, MONTH` only (`app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/domain/model/AnalysisPeriod.kt:8-12`), rendered as a row of `IponFilterChip`s (`AnalysisScreen.kt:220-230`, labels "Day"/"Week"/"Month" at lines 582-586) plus a prev/next `PeriodStepper` (`AnalysisScreen.kt:98,242-251`) that steps an anchor `LocalDate` to the previous/next calendar day, week, or month. `AnalysisWindow` (`.../domain/model/AnalysisWindow.kt:11-15`) is already a generic half-open `[startInclusive, endExclusive)` `Instant` range, and `AnalysisPeriodRange.windowFor`/`.step` (`.../domain/usecase/AnalysisPeriodRange.kt:20-46`) compute calendar-aligned boundaries from the anchor date. `AnalysisCalculator.analyze(transactions, window)` filters the already-loaded transaction stream in memory against that window — there's no SQL date-range query to extend. **Bottom line: the filtering layer already supports arbitrary date ranges; adding the new granularities is additive to the enum + window calculation, no data-fetching changes needed.**

**Decisions (locked in during the 2026-07-04 grilling session):**
1. **Not a semantic shift at all — an extension.** Alvin's actual intent was *more steppable calendar buckets*, not crypto-style trailing windows: `DAY, WEEK, MONTH` gain `QUARTER, SEMI_ANNUAL, ANNUAL, ALL_TIME`, all pageable via the same `PeriodStepper` mechanism (Quarter steps between calendar quarters, Year between calendar years, etc.). There is no trailing-window mode at all — no "last 3 months ending today" concept anywhere in this design. Short, crypto-style-looking labels (exact copy TBD at build time, e.g. abbreviations in the spirit of "1D/1W/1M/3M/6M/12M/All") are used purely for layout compactness — they do **not** imply trailing-window meaning, which is a deliberate, documented deviation from that label convention's usual meaning elsewhere (see ADR-0030).
2. **All-time's window start:** a fixed, arbitrarily-early `Instant` (e.g. year 2000), not a query for the user's actual earliest transaction. No realistic perf concern at this app's data volumes.
3. **Visual redesign of `PeriodSelector`:** replace the `IponFilterChip` row with a lightweight, single-row segmented tab control (think Material3 `TabRow`/`ScrollableTabRow` styling — plain text + underline/pill highlight on the selected item, no chip border/padding/elevation) so all 7 options fit in one compact row instead of wrapping to two rows or needing a dropdown. Wrap it in a horizontally-scrollable row as a safety net for narrow devices or large system font sizes. The existing `PeriodStepper` prev/next row is unchanged — it still steps within whichever bucket type is selected.

**Files likely touched:** `AnalysisPeriod.kt` (add `QUARTER, SEMI_ANNUAL, ANNUAL, ALL_TIME`), `AnalysisPeriodRange.kt` (`.windowFor`/`.step` for each new bucket type), `AnalysisScreen.kt` (`PeriodSelector` redesigned as a scrollable tab row; `PeriodStepper` unchanged), `AnalysisViewModel.kt`.

**Tests to add:** yes for the window-calculation math (`AnalysisPeriodRange.windowFor` for each new preset, especially `ALL TIME`'s edge case) — pure Kotlin, fits CLAUDE.md's "analysis aggregations" tier-1 testing bar.

## Item 12 — Optional "transfer fee" field on transfer transactions

- **Status:** DONE `a41c154` — built, compiles green (`testStagingDebugUnitTest`: 601 tests, 0 failures, incl. new `SaveTransferUseCaseTest.kt` (7) and `DeleteTransactionUseCaseTest.kt` (3), plus additions to `TransactionEditorReducerTest`/`TransactionMapperTest`/`AccountBalanceCalculatorTest`; `assembleStagingDebug` also green), Room bumped to v19 (`AutoMigration(18, 19)`, additive nullable column, same shape as `attachmentUrl`). Confirmed on-device by Alvin (add/edit/clear a transfer fee, delete cascade). See ADR-0031 and the `Transfer fee` glossary term in `CONTEXT.md`.
- **Severity:** N/A (new feature)
- **Suggested model:** Sonnet, low-med — though the scope is now the heavier linked-transaction direction, not the original plain-field recommendation, so budget accordingly

**Built as:** the design decided against a persisted "old fee id" resurrection scheme — new `SaveTransferUseCase` (`feature/transactions/domain/usecase/`) always **retires the previous linked fee (if any) and mints a fresh one** on every transfer save, rather than editing the old row in place. This sidesteps a real correctness trap: `TransactionRepositoryImpl.upsertTransaction()` preserves an existing row's `isDeleted` flag across edits (by design, so a generic upsert can never silently resurrect a tombstone) — which would have silently kept a re-added fee dead forever if the same id were reused after being cleared. Delete-old-then-mint-new avoids that entirely at the cost of a few extra harmless tombstones per edited fee, consistent with ADR-0010's "tombstones kept indefinitely" stance. `Transaction.transferFeeTransactionId: String?` is the only new domain field — no reverse pointer on the fee-expense row is needed since nothing ever needs to look up "which transfer owns this fee" starting from the fee side.

`SaveTransferUseCase` also lazily seeds a "Transfer fees" category on first use, deterministic per user (`DeterministicUuid.v5("builtin-category:transfer-fee:$userId")`, same idempotent-seed pattern as onboarding's `SeedStarterDataUseCase`) — icon reuses the existing `"bills"` (Receipt) key, no new icon added. **Scope decision:** this category is a normal, visible category once created — selectable in the picker grid and editable/deletable from the Categories screen like any other. ADR-0031's "not user-picked" only describes how the *linked fee expense itself* gets categorized (auto-assigned in code, no picker shown for that specific field) — it doesn't require hiding the category everywhere, and adding an `isBuiltIn`/protected-category concept for this alone was judged more machinery than the ADR asks for. Accepted, documented consequence: if a user manually deletes "Transfer fees" from the Categories screen, future fee-linked expenses still save correctly (balance/Analysis math is untouched — categoryId is just a label) but display as "Uncategorized" until the user recreates a category and nothing re-links to it automatically.

`DeleteTransactionUseCase` now cascades one-directionally: before deleting any row, it reads the row and — only if it has a non-null `transferFeeTransactionId` (true only for transfers, by construction) — retires that linked fee first. A fee-expense itself never carries this field, so deleting a fee-expense directly from Records is a plain delete with no cascade back to its parent transfer (the accepted edge case above already covers what happens if a user does this instead of clearing the fee via the transfer's own editor).

`TransactionEditorReducer` gained a `TransferFeeInvalid` `BuildResult` case (non-negative check, mirrors `OwedInvalid`) and `Ready.transferFee: BigDecimal?` (always non-null for a TRANSFER — blank text defaults to `ZERO`, meaning "no fee" — so every transfer save routes through `SaveTransferUseCase`, never the plain `upsertTransaction` path). `onType` clears `transferFeeText` when switching away from TRANSFER, mirroring how `categoryId`/`toAccountId` are already normalized on type switches. `AddTransactionViewModel` tracks the loaded transfer's `existingTransferFeeId` as a private var (persisted through `SavedStateHandle` alongside the rest of the draft, so a process-death mid-edit still retires the correct old row on resume) and, when editing an existing transfer, fetches the linked fee's current amount via the existing `GetTransactionUseCase` to prefill the field — no new repository method needed. UI: a "Transfer fee (₱, optional)" field appears in `AddTransactionScreen.kt` right under "To account," with a supporting caption explaining it's recorded as a separate expense.

**Files touched:** `Transaction.kt` (+`transferFeeTransactionId`), `TransactionEntity.kt`/`TransactionDto.kt`/`TransactionMapper.kt` (thread the new field), `TransactionRepositoryImpl.kt` (`upsertTransaction` carries it through), `IponDatabase.kt` (v18→v19, `AutoMigration(18,19)`), `supabase/schema.sql` (+`transfer_fee_transaction_id uuid`, no FK — same pull-order-tolerance rationale as the table's other omitted FKs) + new `supabase/migrations/2026-07-04_transfer_fee.sql`; new `SaveTransferUseCase.kt`; `DeleteTransactionUseCase.kt` (cascade); `TransactionEditorReducer.kt`/`TransactionEditorState.kt` (`transferFeeText`/`transferFeeError`, `TransferFeeInvalid`, `Ready.transferFee`); `AddTransactionViewModel.kt` (wiring, prefill, SavedStateHandle); `AddTransactionScreen.kt` (new field). New tests: `SaveTransferUseCaseTest.kt`, `DeleteTransactionUseCaseTest.kt`; extended `TransactionEditorReducerTest.kt`, `TransactionMapperTest.kt`, `AccountBalanceCalculatorTest.kt`.

**Migration applied live** (2026-07-04, Alvin, staging Supabase SQL Editor) — `transfer_fee_transaction_id` now exists on the live `transactions` table. The transfer-with-fee row saved during on-device testing (before the migration landed) had been stuck `pending_sync = true` per the analysis above; the next sync cycle after applying flushes it automatically, no manual fix needed.

**Verify on-device (Alvin):** create a transfer, add a fee, confirm a second "Transfer fees"-categorized expense appears in Records for the fee amount and that it shows up in Analysis's expense total/category breakdown; edit the transfer to change the fee and confirm the old fee-expense is gone and a new one reflects the new amount; clear the fee to blank/0 and confirm the linked expense disappears; delete the transfer entirely and confirm the linked fee-expense is also gone (check Records, not just the transfer).

**Current transfer data model, confirmed by reading the code:** a transfer is **one** `Transaction` row, not two paired rows. `TransactionType` is `INCOME, EXPENSE, TRANSFER` (`app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/model/TransactionType.kt:7-10`). `Transaction` (`.../domain/model/Transaction.kt:18-38`) has a single `accountId` (source) plus optional `toAccountId` (destination, line 23); `amount` is always a positive magnitude. `AccountBalanceCalculator.balances()` (`.../domain/usecase/AccountBalanceCalculator.kt:41-49`) posts `-amount` to `accountId` and `+amount` to `toAccountId` from that one row — confirms there's no second linked row the way partner-debt settlements work (ADR-0019's linked-transaction pattern, `isSettlement` flag on `Transaction.kt:37`, is a different, heavier mechanism used elsewhere).

**Existing "conditional field on type" pattern to follow:** `AddTransactionScreen.kt:237-251` already shows a "To account" `ChipRow` only `if (editor.type == TransactionType.TRANSFER)`, else the Category grid. A "Transfer fee" field slots into the same `if` block. `TransactionEditorReducer.onType` (`.../presentation/TransactionEditorReducer.kt:32-40`) already nulls `categoryId` on switching to `TRANSFER` and nulls `toAccountId` on switching away — a `transferFee` field would follow the same null-on-switch-away handling. `TransactionValidator.kt:48-52` already has type-conditional validation (`DESTINATION_REQUIRED` for `TRANSFER` only) to extend if the fee needs its own validation (e.g. non-negative).

**Decisions (locked in during the 2026-07-04 grilling session):** Alvin wants the fee visible in Analysis's expense totals and category breakdown, which rules out the plain-field direction (`AnalysisCalculator` only sees category-tagged rows; a `TRANSFER` row isn't one). Going with the heavier linked-transaction direction instead — deliberately diverging from the ADR-0019 settlement pattern it superficially resembles:
1. A non-zero transfer fee spawns a **second, linked `EXPENSE` transaction**, not a plain field on the transfer row.
2. That linked expense gets a **new, dedicated, auto-assigned built-in category** (e.g. "Transfer fees") — not user-picked, and not left uncategorized (which `TransactionValidator.kt:46`'s `CATEGORY_REQUIRED` wouldn't allow anyway without a waiver).
3. **No `is_settlement` flag** — that flag makes Analysis *exclude* a row (a repayment isn't spending); a transfer fee is real incidental spending and must be *included*, which is the entire point of choosing this direction over the plain field.
4. **Cascades with its parent transfer**, unlike the settlement pattern's fire-and-forget debt link: editing the transfer's fee amount updates the linked expense, and deleting the transfer soft-deletes the linked expense too. Without this, a deleted transfer would leave an orphaned fee-expense still silently affecting balance and Analysis totals.
5. Validation: non-negative only — no ceiling, no "must be less than the transferred principal" rule.

**Files likely touched:** `Transaction.kt`, `TransactionEditorState.kt`/`TransactionEditorReducer.kt`, `AddTransactionScreen.kt` (conditional field near lines 237-251), `AccountBalanceCalculator.kt` (linked expense affects balance, not a fee deduction on the transfer row itself), `TransactionValidator.kt`, `TransactionRepositoryImpl` (cascade create/update/delete of the linked expense), `TransactionMapper.kt` (Entity↔Domain↔DTO), a new built-in category seed, `supabase/schema.sql` (link column, mirroring ADR-0019's `source_transaction_id`-style reference).

**Tests to add:** yes — the linked-expense creation/cascade logic and `AccountBalanceCalculator`'s handling of the fee are money math, a hard requirement per CLAUDE.md's testing policy.

2. **Default pins: Notes stays out of `DEFAULT_PINS`**, living in the More sheet by default — same precedent as Savings (ADR-0025). A fresh install's 3 default pins (Analysis, Records, Manage) are unchanged.
3. **Back-button behavior resolved by ADR-0033**, not decided separately here: Notes becomes a `Module graph` like every other module (uniform nesting per Item 14), so it automatically loses its back arrow and gains reset-on-retap for free — no Notes-specific nav logic needed.

**What's wrong, confirmed by reading the code:** `NavRegistry.NOTES` (`NavDestination.kt:55`) already exists as a full `NavDestination` (own icon, own route) but is deliberately excluded from `NavRegistry.all` (`NavDestination.kt:66-68`) — so it's invisible everywhere the registry drives UI: not in the More sheet, not pinnable in the navbar editor. The only way to reach Notes today is a single `Edit`-icon `IconButton` in `TransactionsScreen`'s `TopAppBar` (`TransactionsScreen.kt:96-97`, `onOpenNotes` wired at `IponApp.kt:193`), which pushes `NOTES.route` on top of Records in the flat `NavHost`. This buries an entire V1 feature (rich-text notes, checklists, images, partner sharing) behind an unlabeled icon inside a different module's header, discoverable only by someone who already knows it's there.

**Fix:** add `NOTES` to `NavRegistry.all` (alongside `RECORDS, ANALYSIS, MANAGE, COUPLE, SETTINGS, CALCULATOR, SAVINGS`) so it gets a real presence in the More sheet and becomes pinnable via the navbar editor like every other module. Remove the `Edit` `IconButton` + `onOpenNotes` plumbing from `TransactionsScreen`'s `TopAppBar` and from `IponApp.kt:191-196`.

**Superseded by the decisions above:** the registry-ordering and back-button open questions originally left here are resolved — see "Decisions locked in."

**Files likely touched:** `NavDestination.kt` (add `NOTES` to `all`), `TransactionsScreen.kt` (remove Notes icon/param), `IponApp.kt` (remove `onOpenNotes` wiring), `NotesScreen.kt` (drop the back arrow if built after Item 14 lands).

**Tests to add:** none — registry/wiring change only, verify by running (Notes appears in the More sheet + navbar editor, pinnable, header icon gone from Records).
